cases.description: When the ATRIndicator is constructed with an empty BarSeries (0 bars), getUnstableBars() should return 0, indicating no unstable bars.
When the ATRIndicator is constructed with a BarSeries containing 5 bars, getUnstableBars() should return 5, matching the bar count.
When the ATRIndicator is constructed with a BarSeries containing 42 bars, getUnstableBars() should return 42, verifying correct propagation of the bar count.
When the ATRIndicator is constructed with a large BarSeries (1000 bars), getUnstableBars() should return 1000, ensuring the method works for high counts.

If the underlying BarSeries reports a negative bar count (which is invalid), getUnstableBars() should propagate the error, typically by throwing an IllegalArgumentException or similar. This case verifies defensive handling of corrupt state.
Create an ATRIndicator with a BarSeries of 3 bars, then add 2 more bars to the series. getUnstableBars() should reflect the updated total (3 + 2 = 5).
Start with an empty BarSeries, add 7 bars after the indicator is constructed. The method must return the current bar count (7).

Construct the indicator with a series of 8 bars, then replace its underlying BarSeries with a new series containing 4 bars. getUnstableBars() should now return 4, proving that the method always queries the current series.
Pass a null BarSeries to the ATRIndicator constructor. Subsequent call to getUnstableBars() should throw NullPointerException (or the constructor itself should).

group: ATRIndicator.getUnstableBars() - mocked negative count after construction

cases.description: Create the indicator with a valid series (5 bars) then, using a mock or test double, force getBarCount() to return -3. getUnstableBars() must propagate an IllegalArgumentException, confirming defensive checks for corrupted state.
Construct the indicator with a BarSeries whose size equals Integer.MAX_VALUE. getUnstableBars() should correctly return this maximum value without overflow.
